oi.text: The largest component of the Company’s operating income is NII, which is the difference between interest earned on loans and investments and the interest paid on deposits and other sources of funds (i.e., borrowings). The Company’s level of net interest income can fluctuate over time due to changes in the level and mix of earning assets and sources of funds (volume), and changes in the yield earned and costs of funds (rate). A portion of the Company’s income from loans to local municipalities and from tax-exempt municipal investment securities is not subject to income taxes. Because the proportion of tax-exempt items in the Company's balance sheet varies from year-to-year, to improve comparability of information, the non-taxable income shown in the tables below has been converted to a tax equivalent basis. The Company’s corporate tax rate is 21%; therefore, to equalize tax-free and taxable income in the comparison, we divide the tax-free income by 79%, with the result that every tax-free dollar is equivalent to $1.27 in taxable income for the periods presented.

prov.text:
The credit loss expense was made up of the following components for the periods indicated:

The increase in the credit loss expense on loans for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to the same period of 2025 was due in part to changes in the economic forecast, prepayments speeds, and loan curtailments, as well as an increase of $127 thousand to the reserve for an individually analyzed commercial loan that is in workout. The increase in the credit loss expense on loans for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to the same period in 2025 was due to the factors listed above as well as an adjustment to certain qualitative factors in the first quarter of 2026 and growth of the loan portfolio. The decrease in the OBS credit exposure for the three months ended September 30, 2026, is attributable to a decrease in unfunded commitments and the increase in the nine months ended September 30, 2026, is attributable to an increase in unfunded commitments year over year.

ACL and provisions –The Company’s ACL policy provides guidance in maintaining an adequate methodology for establishing, estimating, and maintaining allowances for credit losses under ASC 326.

pretax.text: The provision for income taxes increased $60,989, or 6.1%, for the third quarter of 2026 and $440,964, or 17.7%, for the first nine months of 2026 compared to the same periods in 2025, which is consistent with the increase in income before income taxes. Tax credits, which consist of credits from affordable housing investments and NMTC, amounted to $307,236 and $249,612 for the third quarter of 2026 and 2025, respectively and $1,228,944 and $998,448, for the first nine months of 2026 and 2025, respectively.

tax.heading: APPLICABLE INCOME TAXES
tax.text:
The provision for income taxes increased $60,989, or 6.1%, for the third quarter of 2026 and $440,964, or 17.7%, for the first nine months of 2026 compared to the same periods in 2025, which is consistent with the increase in income before income taxes. Tax credits, which consist of credits from affordable housing investments and NMTC, amounted to $307,236 and $249,612 for the third quarter of 2026 and 2025, respectively and $1,228,944 and $998,448, for the first nine months of 2026 and 2025, respectively.

Amortization expense related to the affordable housing investments and NMTC is included as a component of income tax expense and amounted to $257,433 and $638,604, respectively, for the first quarter of 2026 and 2025 and $772,299 and $638,604, respectively, for the first nine months of 2026 and 2025. These investments provide tax benefits, including tax credits, and are designed to provide a targeted effective annual yield between 5% and 7%.

net.text: Consolidated net income for the third quarter of 2026 increased $343,828, or 7.2%, to $5.1 million compared to $4.7 million for the same quarter of 2025, and increased $1.8 million, or 14.7%, to $14.1 million for the first nine months of 2026 compared to $12.3 million for the same period in 2025. The increases in net interest income after credit loss expense of $930,133 for the third quarter of 2026 and $3.4 million for the first nine months of 2026, compared to the respective periods in 2025, were contributing factors to the increases in net income. These changes, along with significant changes in non-interest income and non-interest expense, are discussed in the appropriate sections of this Management’s Discussion and Analysis.

Net interest income.text: Interest Rate Risk and Asset and Liability Management - Management actively monitors and manages the Company’s interest rate risk exposure and attempts to structure the balance sheet to maximize net interest income while controlling its exposure to interest rate risk. The Company's ALCO is made up of the Executive Officers and certain Vice Presidents of the Bank representing major business lines. The ALCO formulates strategies to manage interest rate risk by evaluating the impact on earnings and capital of such factors as current interest rate forecasts and economic indicators, potential changes in such forecasts and indicators, liquidity and various business strategies. The ALCO meets at least quarterly to review financial statements, liquidity levels, yields and spreads to better understand, measure, monitor and control the Company’s interest rate risk. In the ALCO process, the committee members apply policy limits set forth in the Asset Liability, Liquidity and Investment policies approved and periodically reviewed by the Company’s Board of Directors (together the ”ALCO Policy”).

intro.text: Community Bancorp. is the parent holding company for Community National Bank, headquartered in Derby, Vermont. Community National Bank is an independent bank that has been serving its communities since 1851, with retail banking offices located in Derby, Derby Line, Island Pond, Barton, Newport, Troy, St. Johnsbury, Montpelier, Barre, Lyndonville, Morrisville and Enosburg Falls as well as loan offices located in Burlington, Vermont and Lebanon, New Hampshire

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Short-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for the cash they will return: financial.

lines.name: Debt securities
lines.why: Bonds held for sale or to maturity: financial.

lines.name: Loans, net of the allowance
lines.why: Lending is a bank's business: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Deposits
lines.why: Customers' money a bank holds is its business: operating.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.
